heading.title: My experience
heading.text: I trained as an engineer in Mumbai, took a part-time editing job in 2021 and never went back. Five years at Bharat in Germany took me from cutting shorts to running content and producing. Since December 2025 I edit full time as a freelancer. Still climbing.

moments.title: IIT Engineering at VESIT, Mumbai
moments.line: Plan A did not happen. Plan B was four years of engineering.

moments.label: Feb 2021
moments.title: First editing job
moments.line: Part-time short form editor at Bharat in Germany, while finishing the degree.

moments.label: Jun 2021
moments.title: Graduated, went full time
moments.line: The degree was done. Editing became the job.

moments.label: Jan 2022
moments.title: Social media manager
moments.line: From cutting the videos to running the channels they went out on.

moments.label: Sep 2022
moments.title: Started making my own
moments.line: YouTube videos and Reels, from the idea to the upload.

moments.label: Jan 2023

moments.label: Jun 2024

moments.label: Dec 2025

caption.title: Olympus Mons, Mars
caption.line: The tallest mountain known in the solar system.
caption.credit: Image: NASA / JPL-Caltech / USGS / Arizona State University

places.name: Olympus Mons
places.line: A mons, 610.13 km across. The name was approved in 1973.

places.name: Olympus Paterae
places.line: The summit patera group, 85 km across. The name was approved in 2017.

places.name: Zeus Patera
places.line: A patera 65 km across, named for the Greek god of sky, thunder and lightning, king of the gods of Mount Olympus.

places.name: Hera Patera
places.line: A patera 32 km across, named for the Greek goddess of women and marriage, wife of Zeus.

places.name: Olympus Rupes
places.line: The scarp that rings the mountain, up to 6 km high.

places.name: Pangboche
places.line: A crater 10.16 km across, named for a village in Nepal.

places.name: Karzok
places.line: A crater 15.29 km across, named for a village in Kashmir.

places.name: Nix Olympica
places.line: An albedo feature name meaning Snows of Olympus, approved in 1958.

facts.text: 27 kilometers high, over 600 kilometers across at its base.
It is the largest known volcano in the Solar System.
A well-defined scarp, up to 6 kilometers high, surrounds the volcano.
The summit caldera is almost 3 kilometers deep and 25 kilometers across.
Much of the plains around the volcano are covered by a ridged and grooved aureole. Its origin is controversial.
